replication.target_description: Replication target effect: agreement with knowledge ascription in randomly assigned thief/person versus jewel/object contrast conditions, assessed by the reported between-condition t-test. Only n_r and reported_success assigned; es/p are unassigned placeholders.

n.sample_role: Participants in two mutually exclusive randomized target conditions: 74 thief/person and 76 jewel/object.
n.exclusions: Results list 74 and 76 for the target groups. Methods report 150 recruited and 13 failed to complete; source does not reconcile this with the target-group counts. No further analytic exclusions specified.
n.location: Results > Data analysis - Target effect; group means and Ns (canonical DOCX text; no page markers)
n.quote:
The mean rating in the first case (thief/person contrast condition) was 6.21 (N=74 and SD=1.037).
The mean rating in the second case (jewel/object contrast condition) was 5.34 (N=76 and SD=1.837).

reported_success.location: Discussion > Success assessment; response to question whether replication succeeded and original team agrees

notes: Identity assessed from content: source header identifies OSF download k2cna and PostReplication Form - Schaffer and Knobe draft v0.2 DOCX. It names Contrastive Knowledge Surveyed, Schaffer and Knobe, Noûs 46(4), 675–708, and replication team José V. Hernández-Conde, Kareem Khalifa, Daniel Wilkenfeld. Original reference year is 2012 here versus 2010 in the supplied reference; title, journal volume and pages match. Replication-team names and target design match the assigned reference/locator. This is a primary completed replication report with Methods, Results and Discussion, not merely a registry/preregistration. Text does not print the registry DOI or establish its date. No PDF supplied. Analytic N arithmetic: 74 + 76 = 150, using mutually exclusive randomized target groups explicitly listed in Results. This is not recruitment-minus-attrition arithmetic. Methods state 150 recruited and 13 failed to complete, inconsistent with target results Ns; retain this discrepancy for parent review. Unassigned original/es/p fields are placeholders, not absence findings.
